I now have full context. The correctness reviewer (same round) flagged R5-COR-MAJ-002 (make_output_dir leak) and R5-COR-MIN-002 (--expected-wrapper-sha silently accepted in --restore). I can cross-reference these and focus on the safety-bypass angle. Producing the output now.

Two MAJ, one MIN, two nit. All three prior MAJ (SAFE-001 degradation-acknowledgement guard, SAFE-002 APPLY_FAIL audit-trap, SAFE-003 exactly-one log-entry assertion) are confirmed closed. Fail-closed default, blocked-on-adopter-conflict negative assertion, CI=true bootstrap-guard ordering, and parse_entry_repo cardinality check all verified correct. New MAJ-001: scaffold-downstream.sh system-path restriction uses raw string case-pattern matching without path normalisation; `..`-traversal bypass allows e.g. `--output-dir /home/user/../../etc` to resolve to a system directory while passing the case guard. New MAJ-002: ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 3 continues to present `--expected-wrapper-sha` as optional ('If you want'); Gate 2→Gate 3 ordering remains documentation-only with no machine enforcement, leaving the break-glass gate structure bypassable under pressure. MIN-001 (overlaps R5-COR-MAJ-002): test make_output_dir leaks `out.XXXXXX` dirs under REPO_ROOT — confirmed by git status showing out.KUChNE/ and out.xHr6c6/ as untracked artifacts; from a safety angle, those dirs contain wrapper YAML and manifest JSON with real SHAs and adopter repo identifiers outside the test tmp scope. Two nit: --expected-wrapper-sha silently accepted alongside --restore and ignored (overlaps R5-COR-MIN-002); punctuation-only 20-char TF descriptions pass CI by design.","findings":[{"id":"SAFE-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"scaffold-downstream.sh system-path deny list (lines 131-135) uses raw string case-pattern matching without path normalisation, allowing --output-dir paths containing `..` sequences to bypass all denials while the kernel silently resolves them to protected directories.","evidence":"Lines 127-135: `-d \"$OUTPUT_DIR\"` and `-w \"$OUTPUT_DIR\"` evaluate via kernel path resolution (resolves `..`), but `case \"$OUTPUT_DIR\" in /etc|/etc/*|/var|/var/*|...` matches the raw unresolved literal string. `--output-dir /home/user/../../etc` passes `-d` (resolves to /etc on the filesystem), does not match any literal pattern, and proceeds to mkdir + emit 4 files. No `realpath`/`readlink -f` normalisation precedes the case check.","impact":"On containerised or misconfigured environments where /etc or /var is writable by the operator user, the scaffolder emits policy-check-wrapper.yml, CODEOWNERS-snippet.txt, CASCADE-PR-BODY.md, and MANIFEST.json into a system directory. The protection is silently defeated; no warning is emitted. Violates D-044's operational contract that the output-dir guard is a meaningful safety boundary.","mitigation":"Before the case check, normalise: `OUTPUT_DIR=\"$(readlink -f \"$OUTPUT_DIR\" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' \"$OUTPUT_DIR\")\"`. The case pattern then catches traversal-resolved paths. Add a companion test: `--output-dir \"$(mktemp -d \"$TMPDIR/tr.XXXXXX\")/../../etc\"` expecting exit 1."},{"id":"SAFE-MAJ-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 3's dependency on Gate 2 completion is advisory-only. The `--expected-wrapper-sha` flag is presented as optional ('If you want the helper to enforce...'), leaving no machine enforcement that the wrapper was re-pinned to a release-tag SHA before re-arming the required check after break-glass.","evidence":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 3.0: 'If you want the helper to enforce that comparison for you, pass `--expected-wrapper-sha <release-tag-sha-from-gate-2>`'. The R4-archive SAFE-007 prompted adding this flag; it exists in enable-required-check.sh (lines 195-198) but remains opt-in. An operator can invoke forward-mode re-enable without `--expected-wrapper-sha` and the script proceeds regardless of the adopter wrapper's pinned SHA.","impact":"Break-glass scenario: operator completes Gate 1 (disable via --restore), skips Gate 2 (wrapper re-pin), proceeds to Gate 3 (re-enable). The required check re-arms with the adopter wrapper still pinned to the defective SCP SHA, perpetuating the defect that triggered break-glass. This defeats the three-gate structure invariant in plan-doc §2 inv.7 and §12.8's rationale paragraph.","mitigation":"Change §12.8 Gate 3 language from 'If you want the helper to enforce...' to 'REQUIRED: pass `--expected-wrapper-sha <release-tag-sha-from-gate-2>` — do not re-enable without it.' In enable-required-check.sh, consider making --expected-wrapper-sha mandatory when a prior invocation log entry exists for the target repo, or at minimum promote the flag to a REQUIRED step in Gate 3.1 narrative."},{"id":"SAFE-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh make_output_dir() creates test output directories under REPO_ROOT (not TMPDIR); the EXIT trap covers only $TMPDIR, leaving wrapper YAML and MANIFEST.json artifacts containing real SHAs and adopter repo identifiers uncontrolled outside the test sandbox. Confirmed by git status showing out.KUChNE/ and out.xHr6c6/ as untracked REPO_ROOT entries.","evidence":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh lines 85-87: `make_output_dir() { mktemp -d \"${REPO_ROOT}/out.XXXXXX\"; }`. EXIT trap at lines 9-13: `cleanup() { rm -rf \"$TMPDIR\"; }`. R4-archive SAFE-006 fixed tmp_deny_dir (now uses $TMPDIR/deny.XXXXXX at line 151) but did not address make_output_dir. git status at conversation open confirms two persisting test dirs from prior runs with unconfined repo/SHA content.","impact":"Leaked dirs accumulate per test run; each contains policy-check-wrapper.yml with the actual SCP_SHA and adopter repo string, and MANIFEST.json with SHA256 fingerprints. While not credential material, these constitute uncontrolled test artefacts visible in git status to all contributors and potentially captured by CI artefact collectors. Overlaps R5-COR-MAJ-002 but elevated in this lens because of the manifest content.","mitigation":"Change make_output_dir to `mktemp -d \"${TMPDIR}/out.XXXXXX\"` — the existing EXIT trap then covers all test artefacts without further change. Add `out.*/` to .gitignore as belt-and-suspenders against any future divergence."},{"id":"SAFE-nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"`--expected-wrapper-sha` is silently accepted alongside `--restore` and ignored; the standalone-mode incompatibility check at line 210 does not include `[ -n \"$EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA\" ]`, so an operator copy-pasting from Gate 3 documentation into a Gate 1 invocation gets no feedback that the SHA check is skipped.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh line 210: incompatibility guard checks REPO, BRANCH, PLAN_ONLY, ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS, ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI, ENFORCE_ADMINS — but not EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA. Arg parser at line 195-198 sets EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA. restore_branch_protection() never reads it. Combined `--restore file.json --expected-wrapper-sha abc123` parses silently as restore-only. Overlaps R5-COR-MIN-002.","impact":"An operator following §12.8 who passes `--expected-wrapper-sha` during a --restore invocation receives no error and may believe the SHA pin was verified. Low probability in practice since the flags serve opposite phases of break-glass.","mitigation":"Add `|| [ -n \"$EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA\" ]` to the standalone-mode guard at line 210, producing: `error: --restore is a standalone mode and cannot be combined with forward-mode flags`."},{"id":"SAFE-nit-002","severity":"nit","claim":"The TF-024X meaningful-content regex `\\S.{19,}` accepts 20-char all-punctuation descriptions (e.g. `--------------------`), passing CI without any semantic content. This design boundary is not documented in the test harness, leaving the semantic-meaningfulness control invisible to future reviewers.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 203, 218: `\\S.{{19,}}`. test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh case 4g: STATUS.md row with description `--------------------` (20 hyphens) expects exit 0 — confirming by design. Plan-doc §2 inv.2 states 'allows the remaining 19+ chars to be anything'. No comment in case 4g or DISPATCH-NOTE §Cascade-status spec recap notes this boundary. Carry-forward from r4-archive SAFE-010.","impact":"A TF row with 20+ punctuation chars satisfies CI. Semantic meaningfulness falls entirely to human DISPATCH-NOTE review with no CI signal. Acknowledged design limitation; risk is that future maintainers may assume CI enforces content quality.","mitigation":"No code change. Add comment to test case 4g: `# passes by design — regex is a syntactic floor only; semantic content is a human-review control`. Mirror in DISPATCH-NOTE §Cascade-status spec recap."}]}
